Q: finding common characters from an array of words A:

Problem is

letter = ord(w) - ord('a')

which calculate number (and later you get numbers in result)

It should be

letter = w

and this uses letters (and later you get letters in result).

That's all.

Full working code

def original(words):
    dicts = []
    for word in words:
        count = {}

        for w in word:
            #letter = ord(w) - ord("a")
            letter = w
            #print(f"{letter}=")
            count[letter] = count.get(letter, 0) + 1

        dicts.append(count)

    #print(dicts)

    d1 = set(dicts[0].keys())
    #print(d1)

    for d in dicts[1:]:
        d1.intersection_update(set(d.keys()))
    #print(d1)

    res = list(d1)

    return res

# --- main ---

words = "hello world of python".split()

print(original(words))

Result:

['o']

By the way: if you want only "all common characters in a list of word" then I don't undestand why you could letters. You could use directly set(word) and intersection_update in one for-loop.

def my_version(words):
    result = set(words[0])

    for word in words[1:]:
        letters = set(word)
        #print(letters)
        result.intersection_update(letters)

    return list(result)

# --- main ---

words = "hello world of python".split()

print(my_version(words))

Q: WP5 Module Federation: Singleton instantiated multiple times A:

To figure out what goes wrong with your shared you can use undocumented webpack's feature. In your shell app use this code while initing your app:

window.sharedScope = __webpack_require__.S.default;

Then in realtime go to console and look into sharedScope variable (in global scope).

You will see all your shared modules with their versions and source microfrontends. It'll help you to debug your problem.

Also ensure that your shared lib is not bundled into the remoteEntry or (if it is so) check 'eager' option, it should be set to false for remote app and true for shell (or you should check if it is loaded by hands before loading remote app).

Q: Convert RTSP stream to virtual web camera A:

In my experience OBS does not provide good real-time performance, which is mandatory in many applications that need to bind an IP camera to Zoom.

I've been facing this problem for many years.

In the latest Windows version, a new Media Foundation API is available that allows registering a virtual camera.

So I made https://github.com/AndreaGreco/RealTimeWebCam.

It uses FFmpeg to connect to the RTSP stream and tries to be as real-time as possible; in my tests it works at around 100 ms of delay.

Disclaimer: I'm the author, and I'd be glad if other people find my work useful.

Q: Is there a method/constructor in the JDK that creates a JTable with dummy data? A:

You may be thinking of the no-argument JTree() constructor that "Returns a JTree with a sample model." This example illustrates typical usage and result.

For JTable, you can use the JTable constructors suggested here. Alternatively, consider using an implementation of TableModel. This example synthesizes data by extending AbstractTableModel, an abstract class that "provides default implementations for most of the methods in the TableModel interface."
